description: We are a team from Tampa, Florida, made up of college freshmen studying Computer Science and Mechanical Engineering. We’re excited to use this hackathon to gain experience and explore how technology can contribute to space exploration. Although we’re still developing our skills, we’re eager to learn and grow.
summary: Our project is a web-based astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support the physical and mental well-being of astronauts during long-duration space missions. We developed an interactive website with four key features that help astronauts monitor health indicators, recognize potential health concerns, and track changes over time. Each feature addresses specific risks associated with space environments, including microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, and confinement. By presenting health information in an accessible and understandable way, our platform encourages astronauts to take a more active role in monitoring their own health. This directly addresses NASA's challenge of helping astronauts independently recognize and respond to health changes when immediate medical assistance may not be available. Our project is important because early awareness of health concerns can support timely intervention, reduce risks during missions, and improve astronaut safety. Ultimately, we hope to contribute to healthier, safer, and more sustainable human space exploration.
details:
Our project is an interactive, web-based astronaut health monitoring platform designed to help astronauts independently monitor their health during long-duration space missions. The website includes four main features that address different aspects of astronaut health, helping users track vital signs, sleep patterns, mental well-being, and physical activity.

The platform organizes health information into accessible tools that allow astronauts to record measurements, complete self-assessments, and observe changes in their health over time. Its benefits include encouraging early awareness of potential health concerns, making health monitoring more accessible, and promoting greater responsibility for personal well-being when immediate medical assistance may not be available.

Our intended impact is to support safer and healthier long-duration missions, particularly future missions to the Moon and Mars. What makes our project creative is its combination of multiple aspects of astronaut health into one centralized platform rather than focusing on a single medical indicator. During development, our team considered NASA research on microgravity, cardiovascular changes, sleep disruption, muscle deterioration, and behavioral health. We also prioritized scientific accuracy, accessibility, ease of use, and the unique challenges of monitoring health in isolated space environments.

We developed our website using Figma and its AI-assisted features to help design and develop the platform, alongside HTML and CSS for its web structure and styling. NASA research and Human Research Program resources helped guide our selection of health indicators and the scientific foundation of our features.
